newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen flat to down with OTC, cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen flat to down with OTC, cash.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open flat to lower Friday after yesterday's mixed session amid falling western cash power prices and slight break from the scorching heat in the Southwest.

In over-the-counter business, September Palo Verde (PV) futures were quoted at $30.75-31.35 a megawatt hour (MWh) versus Thursday's settlement at $30.95, while September California-Oregon Border (COB) was discussed at 22.75-23.50 against yesterday's close at $23.15.
Firm, peak electricity prices for Saturday/Monday at PV were talked at $35.00-36.00 down from yesterday's $53.00-57.00 and at COB $19.00-20.00 down from $26.00-28.00 Thursday.
Despite downward pressure, market sources said NYMEX price movement could be limited today due to absence of many players who were attending a conference in Vancouver, B.C., this week.
"It's going to be a quiet market. If anything, it'll head lower," one futures trader said.
On the downside, analysts assessed technical support for September PV at $30.00 and for September COB at $22.50.
After pushing power demand to record highs this week, the sizzling heat that smothered most of the Southwest showed signs of losing its grip.

While some interior section of the Southwest were still called to see triple-digit heat today, a cooling trend was expected to take root this weekend and bring temperatures back to seasonal summer levels especially along the coast.

In the Pacific Northwest, descent of an Arctic air mass early next week was forecast to push readings as much as 10 degrees F below normal in western Canada, Montana and Wyoming. The rest of the region was expected to experience near to slightly above normal temperatures.
In generation news, the 220 megawatt (MW) unit 3 at the Four Corners generating complex in New Mexico was expected to resume operation today after being shut Wednesday to repair a boiler tube leak.
Electricity output from the 1,221 MW Palo Verde nuclear power unit 3 in Wintersburg, Ariz., resumed full ouput early Friday after repairs to a condensate pump.
The adjacent 1,221 MW Palo Verde nuclear power unit 2 was operating at 90 percent of capacity as the unit coasts down to a scheduled refueling outage September 6.
The neighboring unit 1, also at 1,221 MW, dipped slightly to 98 percent power as of early Friday.
